explorer.error.notFound: “{name}” no longer exists; the entry or its folder has been removed.
search.limitReached: There are more results; the first {matches} are shown. Narrow your search.
versionControl.selectChange: Select a change in the sidebar to see its diff.
versionControl.status.untracked: new, not yet known to Git
versionControl.binary: “{name}” is a binary file; its diff is not shown.
versionControl.tooLarge: “{name}” is too large to show its diff.
versionControl.history.title: History
versionControl.noRepositoryInWorkspace: No project in this workspace is a Git repository. Running “git init” in a terminal turns a project folder into one.
versionControl.repository.publish: Create the branch of {project} on GitHub and push
versionControl.history.noFiles: This commit changes no file in the project folder.
versionControl.maximizeTooltip: Show version control across the whole main area
versionControl.showTerminalsTooltip: Show the other groups next to version control again
versionControl.gitMissing: Git was not found. Install Git for Windows and restart Kredr to use version control. Everything else works without Git.
versionControl.noRepository: This folder is not a Git repository. Run “git init” in a terminal to make it one.
versionControl.error.timedOut: Git did not respond in time and was stopped.
versionControl.error.authenticationRequi: GitHub requires a sign-in or confirmation. Kredr does not ask for it itself: run “git push” once in a terminal and sign in there. After that it works here too.
versionControl.error.pushRejected: The push was rejected because GitHub has newer commits.
versionControl.error.unreachable: GitHub cannot be reached. Check your internet connection and the address of the repository.
versionControl.error.noRemote: This repository is not connected to a repository on GitHub. Run “git remote add origin <address>” in a terminal to connect it.
versionControl.error.conflict: Merging caused conflicts. The affected files are marked in the list. Resolve the conflicts, for example with an agent, then commit.
versionControl.commitScope.all: Nothing staged: the commit contains all changes.
versionControl.commitScope.staged: The commit contains only the staged changes.
versionControl.publishTooltip: Create the branch on GitHub and push
versionControl.discardConfirm.title: Discard changes?
versionControl.discardConfirm.message: The changes to “{name}” will be lost permanently.
versionControl.discardConfirm.untracked: “{name}” is new and will be moved to the Windows Recycle Bin.
status.unpublishedTooltip: This branch is not on GitHub yet. The first push creates it there.
versionControl.error.localChangesBlockSw: The branch was not switched because switching would overwrite your local changes. Nothing has been lost. Commit or discard the changes, then switch again; the affected files are listed in the original text.
versionControl.error.branchExists: A branch with this name already exists. Pick it from the list or choose a different name.
versionControl.error.invalidBranchName: This is not a valid branch name. Not allowed are, among others, spaces, “..”, “~”, “^”, “:” and a leading hyphen.
branches.tooltip: Current branch: {branch}. Click to switch branches or create a new one.
branches.placeholder: Switch branch or type a name for a new branch
branches.none: No branches yet. Type a name to create one.
settings.language.hint: The language of the interface. Until you choose one, it follows the Windows language.
settings.fontFamily.hint: Applies to terminals and the file view. Separate several fonts with commas; the first one installed is used.
settings.fontSize.hint: In pixels, from {min} to {max}. Applies to terminals and the file view.
settings.defaultShell.hint: The shell a new terminal starts with.
settings.agentCommand.hint: The command “New Agent” uses to start Claude Code. You can add options, for example “claude --continue”. In its terminals, Kredr overrides “claude” with its own function that always runs the installed program, so a “claude” you start yourself becomes an agent too.
settings.notifications.hint: Kredr shows a Windows notification when an agent is waiting for input and the window is not in the foreground. The taskbar button is highlighted even with notifications turned off.
settings.showAssignment.hint: An agent's tab and its card in the agents view show its task: the first input since it started or since the last /clear. On the tab, a custom name takes precedence.
settings.resumeAgents.hint: When a project opens, the agents that were running when it closed start in their place and resume their conversation. When off, their tabs come back as plain terminals.
settings.licenses.hint: Kredr is built on open-source packages. They are listed here with their licenses.
settings.licenses.missing: The list is only created when the installer is built.
start.text: Open a folder as a project to get started.
terminal.startFailed: The terminal could not be started: {details}
terminal.shellMissing: {shell} was not found on this computer. This terminal runs PowerShell instead.
window.title: {project} — Kredr
workspace.label: {name} (Workspace)
workspace.created: “{project}” became the workspace “{name}”. Tabs and agents stay as they are; the saved arrangement of “{added}” is not mixed in.
workspace.alreadyContained: “{project}” is already open in this window.
workspace.openElsewhere: “{project}” is already open in another window. Kredr brought that window to the front; a project is only ever open in one window.
workspace.openElsewhereWorkspace: A project of the workspace “{name}” is already open in another window. Kredr brought that window to the front; a project is only ever open in one window.
workspace.pickProject.agent: Choose a project for the new agent
workspace.pickProject.terminal: Choose a project for the new terminal
workspace.removeConfirm.title: Remove project from workspace?
workspace.removeConfirm.message: At least one agent in “{project}” is still working or waiting for input. Removing the project closes all of its terminals and tabs and interrupts its agents. Their conversations are kept and can be continued when the project is opened again.
workspace.removeConfirm.backgroundMessag: At least one agent in “{project}” still has a running background task. Removing the project closes all of its terminals and tabs and ends the background tasks. The agents' conversations are kept and can be continued when the project is opened again.
workspace.removeUnsaved.message: “{project}” has files with unsaved changes. They are lost when the project is removed.
workspace.empty: This workspace does not contain a project yet.
workspace.moveFailed: Could not save the order of the projects: {details}
workspace.dropFolder: Drop a folder here to add it to the workspace
workspace.closeConfirm.title: Close workspace?
workspace.closeConfirm.unsavedFiles: There are files with unsaved changes. They are lost when the workspace is closed.
workspace.closeConfirm.runningProcess: A process is still running in at least one terminal of this workspace, such as an agent. Closing the workspace ends it.
workspace.closeConfirm.workingAgent: At least one agent is still working. Closing interrupts it; its conversation continues the next time the workspace is opened, but it does not resume working on its own.
workspace.closeConfirm.backgroundAgent: At least one agent still has a running background task. Closing ends it; the conversation continues the next time the workspace is opened, but the background task does not restart.
terminal.closeConfirm.title: Close terminal?
terminal.closeConfirm.message: A process is still running in this terminal. Closing the terminal will end it.
terminal.closeWindowConfirm.title: Close window?
terminal.closeWindowConfirm.message: A process, for example an agent, is still running in at least one terminal of this window. Closing the window will end it.
window.closeFailed: The window stays open because asking about the unsaved changes failed ({details}). Save the files, then close it again.
tab.crashed: Something went wrong in this tab: {details}
agent.name: Agent
agent.closeWindowConfirm.title: Close window?
agent.closeWindowConfirm.message: At least one agent is still working. Closing will interrupt it; its conversation resumes the next time the project opens, but it will not continue working on its own.
agent.closeWindowConfirm.backgroundMessa: At least one agent still has a running background task. Closing the window will end it; the conversation resumes the next time the project opens, but the background task will not restart.
agent.missing: The program “{program}” was not found on the search path. The agent start command was run anyway: if “{program}” is an alias or a function of your shell, the agent is running. If the shell reports an error, install Claude Code or change the agent start command in the settings, then choose “New Agent” again.
